title: UCI 360 Air Quality (gas multisensor device with reference analyzer, Italian city, 2004-2005)
summary: Hourly averaged readings from a gas multisensor device (five metal-oxide sensor responses) co-located with a certified reference analyzer, deployed at road level in a polluted area of an unnamed Italian city. The file has 9,357 rows (the UCI page states 9,358 instances) covering hourly records from 2004-03-10 to 2005-04-04 in the sample, which is the whole file. It carries reference NO2, NOx, CO, benzene and NMHC concentrations plus temperature, relative humidity and absolute humidity, but no traffic counts. Missing values are coded as -200 rather than blank.

quality_notes: Declared has_missing_values = 'no' and missing_values_symbol = null on the UCI page, but the notes say missing values are coded -200 and the sample confirms it.

-200 sentinel counts in the sample: CO(GT) 1592 (non-missing share 0.83), NMHC(GT) 8443 (share 0.098), NOx(GT) 1639, NO2(GT) 1642 (share 0.825), PT08 sensor columns, T, RH and AH 366 each (share 0.961), C6H6(GT) 366 (min -200, 366 negative values, non-missing share reported as 1.0, so the sentinel is not counted as missing by the profiler).
NMHC(GT) is about 90% missing (-200 in 8,443 of 9,357 rows), so it is not usable as a reference series.
Negative values in CO(GT) (91 rows) and T (13 rows) are the -200 sentinel or a real sub-zero temperature; the sample does not separate these. Treat them as sentinels until checked.
Row count: the sample has 9,357 data rows, against 9,358 instances on the UCI page.

Period end conflict: the UCI notes say 'March 2004 to February 2005', but the sample's date range runs to 2005-04-04. The sample is the whole file, so the file's date range is taken from the data (end 2005-04-04); the prose appears out of date.
Time is documented as HH.MM.SS but the sample shows H:00:00 values. The sample shows one record per hour, so this is an hourly grain.
Variable metadata lists the PT08 sensor responses as 'Categorical' type on UCI, but the sample shows them as integers. Treat them as numeric.
Sensor drift and cross-sensitivity are documented as present (De Vito et al. 2008), so the sensor responses are not reliable as stand-ins for the reference analyzers.
No traffic counts are in the file, so need N2 is not met. No clinic data is in the file. The file is only a prototype source for N1 (NO2, NOx) and N3 (T, RH, AH). It does not cover N4 to N6.

The licence conflict (CC BY 4.0 vs research-only and no commercial use) must be resolved before any use in a city production pipeline. The use case's production window is 2024-2025, outside this file's coverage.
